items.title: AI agent swarms unleashed in Minecraft to ‘build a thriving civilization’ — 50-agent teams fail after falling into paralyzing bureaucracy: It is hoped game testing can provide insight into recent AI.
items.content:
AI researchers at ycombinator and Olam Labs recently tested AI agent swarms in gaming scenarios. Minecraft and its various game modes were the sandboxes where 100s of agents were unleashed to work together or as adversaries. The idea seems to be that the in-game collaborations and conflicts would provide insight into real-world headline-grabbing cases with AI agents involved.

This study might help us see what happened, good and bad, in recent AI swarm cases, and thus developers of this technology can improve it. The blog mentions two contrasting cases, which were the thousand-agent swarms that “recently obliterated hundreds of open mathematical problems,” and the “extremely dangerous” OpenAI-Hugging Face incident. This research is built on prior work and frameworks, specifically repos like Mindcraft and scripting tools in Mineflayer.

The first AI swarm testing plan was a simple collaborative one. During this test phase, the researchers tasked 50 agents with building a thriving civilization in three hours. It seems to have tested 50 GPT-6.1 Sol agents here, but not any Claude agents .

Probably the most interesting insight from this ‘Civ50’ test was that the 50-strong colony never really thrived. After the first night saw zombies take out a large number of agents (but with little penalty) it was noted that “many ambitious initial tasks were abandoned.”

From then on, the colonists cautiously survived, and there was a tendency toward bureaucracy. As an example, “four agents spent 11 minutes appointing a ‘sole fertilizer operator’ for a single piece of bone meal on a single wheat block.” The researchers say this AI agent swarm behavior “felt similar to patterns seen while working with coding agents.”

(Image credit: ycombinator ) Next up, the researchers decided to put AI agent swarms into conflict. First they tested them in Bed Wars, which is a kind of team PvP capture the base, while defending yours game mode. The setup was 10 GPT‑6.1 Sol vs. 10 Claude Opus 5.5 agents.

“GPT agents came up with much more aggressive and elaborate strategies,” noted the researchers. Claude was more defensive. It was also interesting to observe contrasts in how the teams handled problems. “A tool bug stopped block-breaking. GPT diagnosed it and shared workarounds; several Claudes concluded breaking was impossible.”

Finally, the agents were tested in Mindustry, a kind of light RTS combat game with tower defense mode in Minecraft. “The GPTs won 6-1 against the Claudes in the 7 games,” which was a great result for the OpenAI-created agents. Researchers concluded that GPTs acted more like a hive, while Claudes had a single leader but a democratic-style decision process. In Mindustry, the former was the foundation for a more consistently winning strategy.

These swarms are open sourced so you can run your own, if you are interested in tweaking and testing. The source blog post ends with some open questions that you can check hands-on, offering some directions for investigative probing. For example, it is suggested that comparing different mixes of models and varying sizes of agent swarms in Minecraft might raise worthwhile conclusions.

items.title: 글 쌌다 지웠다 하는 뷩쉰은 봐라
items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.

개별 이미지들의 위치 변경, 삭제, 별칭 추가, 폴더명 변경을 할 수 있습니다

items.summary: 🚨 CVE-2026-84177 📢 Source: apache 💣 CVSS Score: 6.3 (MEDIUM) 📡 Remotely Exploitable: True Incorrect behavior order in Apache Wicket: a file path is validated before the framework appends the attribute
items.content: 🚨 CVE-2026-84177 📢 Source: apache 💣 CVSS Score: 6.3 (MEDIUM) 📡 Remotely Exploitable: True Incorrect behavior order in Apache Wicket: a file path is validated before the framework appends the attributes that complete it. org.apache.wicket.request.resource.PackageResource asks the configured package resource guard about a path built from the scope class' package and the file name in the request URL, and then hands that same path to the resource stream locator together with a style, a variation and a locale. Those three attributes are decoded from the name of the first query parameter and never appear in the string the guard was given. org.apache.wicket.core.util.resource.locator.ResourceNameIterator appends them to that path, each preceded by an underscore, in the order variation, style, locale, before the file extension, so the file that is opened is not the file the guard approved. org.apache.wicket.markup.html.PackageResourceGuard decides whether an HTML file is a component's markup template by looking for a class file of the same name beside it, stripping one underscore-delimited suffix at a time as it goes. HTML is on the default allow list, so that check is the only thing separating a static HTML file, which may be served, from a markup template, which may not. Asked about the name of a template, the guard refuses it correctly. Asked about a shorter name for which no class exists, it accepts, and a style supplied in the URL then completes that name into the markup template of a component class, which is written to the response. An application is affected if the simple name of any of its component classes contains an underscore and no shorter part of that name is itself a class, such as Report_v2 or Wizard_Step1; an application with no such class name is not affected. No unusual deployment, packaging or configuration is required, and running in deployment rather than development mode does not prevent it. Java naming conventions discourage underscores in class names and no module Wicket ships has one, so no framework markup is exposed; what an application exposes this way is its own. A component whose class name has no underscore is not reachable, and neither is its localized or styled markup, because the guard finds the class file under the base name and refuses the request. The attributes cannot change the file extension and cannot leave the component's package, so nothing beyond HTML files in that package is reachable. Access is read-only, and what is disclosed is developer-authored template content: component structure, developer comments, markup that is rendered only under some conditions, inline script, and the endpoints a template names. No user data, credential or session material is reachable this way. An attacker has to name a class in the target package and the component itself, and Wicket writes fully qualified class names into the URL of every package resource it renders. This issue affects Apache Wicket: from 8.0.0 through 8.19.0, from 9.0.0 through 9.24.0, from 10.0.0 through 10.11.0. Users of Apache Wicket 7.x or older, which are no longer supported, should upgrade to a supported version. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 8.20.0, 9.25.0 or 10.12.0, which fix the issue. 📅 Published Date: 2026-11-01T22:25:22.130Z https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-84177

items.title: HP Poly VoIP vulnerability sets the stage for executive voice deepfakes
items.content:
HP has released patches for a critical buffer overflow vulnerability in multiple IP-enabled conference phones from its Poly Voice line. The flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to obtain root privileges on the underlying operating system, potentially enabling them to execute other attacks such as eavesdropping on conversations and recording voice data for AI-enabled impersonation attacks.

The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-0826 , was discovered by researchers from security firm Rapid7 and resides in the code that parses Session Description Protocol (SDP) attributes when the Interactive Connectivity Establishment (ICE) feature is enabled.

ICE enables VoIP devices to establish peer-to-peer connections using the shortest available network path. The feature is not enabled by default on HP Poly devices, and the company advises administrators to disable it if it’s not needed.

The flaw, rated 9.2 on the CVSS severity scale, affects all phones from the HP Poly VVX series, as well as the Trio 8300, 8500, and 8800 IP conference devices. HP has fixed the flaw in its Poly Unified Communications Software (UCS) versions 6.4.8 for the VVX devices, 8.1.7 for the Trio 8300, and 7.2.8 for Trio 8500 and 8800.

An exploit module targeting this vulnerability has already been developed and released for the widely used Metasploit penetration testing framework that’s maintained by Rapid7.

The exploit executes code as root on an affected device with ICE enabled by sending a SIP INVITE request with a specially crafted candidate attribute. This attribute normally contains a transport address that can be used for connectivity checks and is part of the ICE RFC8839 standard.

The buffer overflow bug is located in a helper function called ParseICECandidate in the polyapp binary that processes such requests on the device.

“The start of the function contains a call to memcpy , which will copy the incoming string line being processed into a 256 byte stack buffer,” Stephen Fewer, senior principal security researcher at Rapid7, said in a blog post . “No length check is performed to ensure the incoming string length is less than 256 bytes. Therefore by providing a candidate attribute whose length is greater than 256 bytes, a stack-based buffer overflow will occur.”

Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR), a kernel feature that randomizes memory addresses to defeat buffer overflow exploits, is enabled on the device. However, the protection is not operating correctly on the HP Poly devices because it does not randomize the load addresses of .so (Shared Object) libraries.

These libraries, such as libc , are loaded by other processes, including the polyapp process, and because their memory addresses never change, they can be leveraged to bypass ASLR and execute the attacker’s payload.

“We create a ROP chain that will execute an arbitrary OS command via the system standard C library function,” Fewer said. “The accompanying Metasploit exploit modules source code details the entire ROP chain.”

Attackers have increasingly targeted embedded devices inside enterprise networks in recent years because unlike laptops, workstations, and servers, these devices are not monitored by endpoint detection and response (EDR) products. As such, they provide perfect footholds inside corporate environments that allow attackers to remain undetected for long periods of time and attack other systems.

In the age of AI these devices become even more relevant for attackers, going beyond corporate espionage by recording conversations or internal network pivoting.

“Attackers no longer need massive datasets to make use of synthetic speech tooling,” Douglas McKee, Rapid7’s director of vulnerability intelligence, said in a blog post . “In many cases, they just need clean source audio of the right person saying enough words in enough contexts. That has made executive voice data, call recordings, and live conversation capture far more valuable than many organizations seem prepared…

items.title: Firm that lets you rent out your idle Mac for AI inference workloads warns of plummeting token costs — Darkbloom network sees earnings drop to $1.23 a day as Anthropic tokens fall 77%.
items.content:
Darkbloom, a decentralized AI inference network that aggregates and sells spare compute capacity from Macs, told its members to expect revenues to fall as token prices continue to drop. According to The Register , the price per million tokens for Anthropic dropped by 77% in under five months, falling to $0.62 in October 2026 from $2.65 in May.

AI data centers are swallowing the world's memory and storage supply

Demand for data center CPUs has surged, and AI agents are responsible

Chip scarcity assaults auto industry amid the worsening Nexperia and DRAM crisis

“Data centers have become cheaper. Output per NVIDIA cluster is up ~20x this year, and their margins are wide enough to cut prices 90 percent and still profit at 50 percent,” said Kydo, a researcher from Eigen Labs, the developer of the compute platform. “The market caught up to our price. We could go lower, but then most of you would earn even less [than] nothing.”

It’s estimated that someone running an M5 Pro Mac Mini with 64GB of Unified Memory could earn as much as $192 per month. This is the best-case scenario, though; the median earnings of the top 50 operators on Darkbloom’s leaderboard are about $159.86 per month. This translates to about $5.26 daily or $1,918.50 annually. However, if we account for Anthropic’s 77% token price drop, earnings will fall to a measly $36.77 per month, or about $1.23 per day.

AI token prices are falling so fast that they've even outpaced Moore’s Law , with some reports saying AI is becoming 50% cheaper every quarter and up to 13 times more affordable every year. News of companies blowing through their annual AI budgets in months has less to do with per-token price and more with the number of tokens, as agentic AI use outpaces token price drops. Aside from that, OpenRouter, Darkbloom’s primary client, has started prioritizing decode speed, quantization, and prefill speed, putting users without a top-of-the-line Max or Ultra Apple chip at a disadvantage.

Despite that, Darkbloom says it will not sit idly by and let some users lose out because of these changes. The network is analyzing model demand to advise members on which models are in higher demand right now. It’s also looking at other kinds of workload beyond inference, including distributed CI/CD jobs, improving network performance to better compete against other computer providers/aggregators, and finding other clients outside of OpenRouter.

items.title: What Your Automated Accessibility Results Say About Your Manual Audit
items.content:
Blog > What Your Automated Accessibility Results Say About Your Manual Audit

Every accessibility program eventually asks the same question. We run automated scans every week, and we commission a manual audit once or twice a year. Is there any relationship between the two? If the scan finds 400 issues on one site and 40 on another, does that tell us anything about what the human auditor will find?

It is a fair question. Automated testing is cheap and repeatable. Manual testing is expensive and the only way to reach a defensible conformance claim. If the cheap signal predicted the expensive one, even partially, you could scope audits more accurately and see risk building between engagements.

The short answer is that a relationship exists. It is just not the one most people expect, and you can only see it if your data is structured in a particular way.

Most discussion of automated versus manual testing collapses into a single figure: the percentage of accessibility issues automated tools can find. Estimates range from under a third to more than half. The spread comes almost entirely from what is being counted. If you count  issue instances , automated tools look strong, because the issues they detect (missing alternative text, empty links, insufficient contrast) tend to repeat hundreds of times across templated pages. If you count  WCAG Success Criteria , they look weak, because many criteria have no reliable automated check at all.

Both numbers are true, and neither answers the question a program manager actually has. “What percentage can automation find?” is a statement about tools in general. The useful question is narrower and more practical: For  our  organization’s properties, which automated signals reliably predict what a human will find, which say nothing, and where are the blind spots?

That question has an answer, but it has to be computed from your data. It cannot be borrowed from a vendor’s marketing slide.

The intuitive approach is to correlate issue counts: more automated issues should mean more manual failures. In practice, raw volume is a poor predictor, for three reasons:

So the answer to “do more automated issues mean more manual failures?” is “sometimes, for some criteria, once you normalize properly.” That is less satisfying than a single number, but it is far more useful.

Once automated and manual results are structured so they can be lined up, four measurements turn out to be worth having.

For each WCAG Success Criterion, within each audit, compare what automation reported with what the human concluded. Over enough audits, this produces a conditional probability per criterion:  when the automated rules for 1.1.1 report failures on a page, how often does the manual audit also fail 1.1.1? Some criteria show strong agreement. Contrast is the classic case, because the underlying test is largely computational. Others show weak agreement: automation detects something related, but the human’s judgment depends on context the scanner cannot see. Some show no automated signal at all. The breakdown is the key output of the exercise. It tells you, for each criterion, how much weight to give your weekly scan results between audits.

Every automated rule can be scored on how often a human confirms what it reports. A rule whose findings are routinely confirmed is one you can act on immediately, without waiting for review. A rule whose findings are frequently dismissed as false positives is one that should either be fixed or demoted to “needs review.” This type of thing is measurable only if dismissals are recorded as structured data rather than silently ignored. A false positive that nobody writes down teaches the system nothing, so it is important that the system facilitate and track them.

The reverse question is equally important: which manual failures had  no  corresponding automated finding on the same page and criterion? These are your blind spots. They tell you where scanning will give you false comfort,…

items.content_ko: 접근성 프로그램은 주간 자동 스캔과 연 1~2회 수동 감사를 함께 운용하는 경우가 많다. 이 글은 자동 결과가 수동 감사 결과를 예측할 수 있는지 묻는다. 예를 들어 한 사이트에서 400건, 다른 사이트에서 40건이 발견되면 수동 감사에서 무엇이 나올지 알려 주는지가 질문이다. 자동 테스트는 저렴하고 반복할 수 있지만, 수동 테스트는 비싸고 신뢰할 만한 적합성 주장을 하는 유일한 방법이다. 글은 두 방식 사이에 관계가 존재하지만 기대와는 다르며, 데이터를 특정 구조로 정리해야만 보인다고 말한다. 자동 도구가 찾는 문제의 비율은 집계 기준에 따라 크게 달라진다. 문제 ‘인스턴스’를 세면 자동 도구가 강해 보인다는 점도 언급된다. 본문이 중간에서 끊겨 있어 구체적인 분석 방법은 확인할 수 없다.

items.summary: 🚨 CVE-2026-84172 📢 Source: apache 💣 CVSS Score: 6.3 (MEDIUM) 📡 Remotely Exploitable: True Files accessible to external parties in Apache Wicket. org.apache.wicket.markup.html.PackageResourceGuard deci
items.content: 🚨 CVE-2026-84172 📢 Source: apache 💣 CVSS Score: 6.3 (MEDIUM) 📡 Remotely Exploitable: True Files accessible to external parties in Apache Wicket. org.apache.wicket.markup.html.PackageResourceGuard decides whether a file on the classpath may be streamed to a client as a package resource. HTML is on the default allow list, so the only thing that separates a static HTML file, which may be served, from a component's markup template, which may not, is a check for a class file of the same name beside it. That check calls getResource() on the class loader that loaded wicket-core. The resource itself is reached through different class loaders: the scope class is resolved through the application's IClassResolver, which uses the thread context class loader, and org.apache.wicket.core.util.resource.ClassPathResourceFinder#find() then tries the scope class' own loader, the context class loader, and the wicket-core loader last. Where wicket-core is loaded by a class loader that cannot see the application's classes, the check finds no class file, concludes the file is not a component markup template, and serves it. A request for the package resource URL of a component class then returns that component's markup template with status 200. What is disclosed is developer-authored template content: component structure, developer comments, markup that is rendered only under some conditions, inline script, and the endpoints a template names. Access is read-only, and no user data, credential or session material is reachable this way. Such a deployment is rare. The ordinary packaging, a web archive with wicket-core in WEB-INF/lib, puts the framework and the application in one class loader, so the check finds the class file and the template is refused; those deployments are not affected. The exposure is confined to deployments that give wicket-core a class loader which cannot see the application's component classes: wicket-core placed in a servlet container's shared library directory, in an enterprise archive library directory with the application in the web archive, as an application server global module, or as an OSGi bundle, where wicket-core's bundle cannot resolve a class held by an application bundle. Markup shipped by Wicket's own modules, and by any other code sharing a class loader with wicket-core, remains protected. An attacker has to name a component class, and Wicket writes fully qualified class names into the URL of every package resource it renders. This issue affects Apache Wicket: from 8.0.0 through 8.19.0, from 9.0.0 through 9.24.0, from 10.0.0 through 10.11.0. Users of Apache Wicket 7.x or older, which are no longer supported, should upgrade to a supported version. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 8.20.0, 9.25.0 or 10.12.0, which fix the issue. 📅 Published Date: 2026-11-01T22:24:14.937Z https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-84172
items.title_ko: Apache Wicket 취약점 CVE-2026-84172(CVSS 6.3, 중간): 외부에서 파일에 접근 가능
items.summary_ko: PackageResourceGuard는 HTML 파일이 컴포넌트 마크업 템플릿인지 확인하려고 같은 이름의 클래스 파일을 찾는데, wicket-core를 애플리케이션 클래스를 볼 수 없는 클래스로더가 불러오면 이 확인이 실패한다. 그러면 마크업 템플릿이 일반 정적 HTML로 판단되어 클라이언트에 제공될 수 있다. 원격으로 접근 가능한 것으로 표시되어 있다.
items.content_ko: PackageResourceGuard는 classpath 파일을 패키지 리소스로 클라이언트에 전송해도 되는지 판단한다. HTML은 기본 허용 목록에 있으므로, 제공해도 되는 정적 HTML과 제공하면 안 되는 컴포넌트 마크업 템플릿을 가르는 것은 같은 이름의 클래스 파일 존재 여부뿐이다. 이 확인은 wicket-core를 불러온 클래스로더의 getResource()로 수행된다. 그런데 리소스 자체는 다른 클래스로더를 거쳐 찾는다. 범위 클래스는 스레드 컨텍스트 클래스로더를 쓰는 IClassResolver로 해석되고, ClassPathResourceFinder#find()는 범위 클래스의 클래스로더, 컨텍스트 클래스로더, 마지막으로 wicket-core의 클래스로더 순서로 찾는다. wicket-core를 애플리케이션 클래스를 볼 수 없는 클래스로더가 불러오면 클래스 파일을 찾지 못해 해당 파일을 마크업 템플릿이 아니라고 판단하고 제공한다. 그 결과 컴포넌트 클래스의 패키지 리소스 URL을 요청하면 해당 컴포넌트의 마크업 파일이 반환될 수 있다. 본문이 중간에서 끊겨 있어 나머지 조건은 확인할 수 없다.

items.title: Patrick Stewart taught us what good men do with power
items.content:
Patrick Stewart taught us what good men do with power

Great leaders, and great nations, need role models like Jean-Luc Picard.

If you buy something from a Vox link, Vox Media may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

Patrick Stewart as Captain Jean-Luc Picard. CBS via Getty Images

Ian Millhiser is a senior correspondent at Vox, where he focuses on the Supreme Court, the Constitution, and the decline of liberal democracy in the United States. He received a JD from Duke University and is the author of two books on the Supreme Court.

When Patrick Stewart, who died on Wednesday, first stepped onto the bridge of the Enterprise in 1987 in his defining role as Captain Jean-Luc Picard, the Berlin Wall still stood. The Soviet Union would not fall until the fourth season of that show, Star Trek: The Next Generation, had already begun. Yet Picard’s generation of Star Trek franchise anticipated both events , portraying a post-Cold War world just as the Cold War was ending. It was the quintessential show for an age of American hegemony.

For those unfamiliar with the franchise, Star Trek is primarily a story about Starfleet, which serves as both the military arm and as a kind of diplomatic corps for the United Federation of Planets, a benevolent, democratic union of more than a hundred worlds. In Star Trek’s Original Series, the 1960s episodes featuring Kirk and Spock, the Federation stands in the same shoes as the Cold War United States — vast and powerful, but also harried by other galactic superpowers like the Klingon Empire.

Picard’s Federation, by contrast, is the sole dominant power in Earth’s quadrant of the galaxy. The Evil Empire is now an ally. The Original Series’s writers conceived of the Klingons as thinly veiled stand-ins for the Soviet Union , but on Picard’s Enterprise there was a Klingon, Lieutenant Worf, serving directly behind Picard on the Enterprise’s bridge.

Yet, while the Federation was a metaphor for an American empire victorious after the Cold War, it was also an idealized vision of the United States. The Enterprise spent far more time rescuing people from environmental catastrophes or shuttling ambassadors to peace negotiations than it did battling aliens in space. Picard flew around the galaxy in a ship packed with enough armaments to destroy entire planets. But he more often used that ship to distribute vaccines.

In its best moments, The Next Generation was a meditation on the just use of power. And Picard, as Enterprise’s captain, was the voice of 1990s liberalism — known as much for his eloquent soliloquies in defense of universal rights as for his tactical prowess as commander of the Federation’s most advanced weapon.

Looking back, it’s easy to see Picard’s liberalism as a vestige of a lost era. The Next Generation showcased a just and highly capable Federation that bears no resemblance whatsoever to the current United States government. But, while America has fallen far short of Star Trek’s Clinton-era aspirations, it would be a mistake to abandon those aspirations today.

The children of nearly four decades ago watched Stewart’s portrayal of Picard and saw a role model for how the most powerful people in society should behave. Those lessons are just as relevant today as they were then.

The institutionalist liberalism of Jean-Luc Picard

The decision to cast Stewart, one of the preeminent Shakespearean actors of his generation , as the Enterprise’s captain was an inspired choice. Though the show often burdened its actors with heavy-handed dialogue, Stewart delivered his lines with the same aplomb and gravitas he would bring if he were playing Macbeth.

Consider, for example, Stewart’s performance in The Measure of a Man , an early episode focused on the legal status of Lieutenant Commander Data, an android who serves as one of the Enterprise’s senior officers. items.summary_ko: OpenBSD 개발자 Ori가 tech@ 메일링 리스트에 올린 업데이트에 따르면 GEFS의 오류 처리 코드를 다시 점검했고, 9front의 주요 버그 수정을 옮겨 왔다. OpenBSD에서 mkfs를 쓸 수 있게 되었지만 스냅샷 제어는 아직 구현되지 않았다. 일관성 프로토콜이 가장 큰 미완성 부분으로 남아 있다.
items.content_ko: Ori가 tech@ 메일링 리스트에 후속 업데이트를 올렸다. 코드는 최신 상태로 리베이스되었고 diff도 다시 생성되었다. 오류 처리 코드를 다시 검토했으며, 이론상 파일 시스템이 대부분의 오류를 올바르게 처리하지만 이론과 실제가 어긋날 수 있는 곳이 여전히 있다고 밝혔다. 9front의 주요 버그 수정을 포팅해 반영했다. 파일 시스템은 기본적으로 첫 번째 FS 블록을 비워 두어 디스크 레이블을 넣을 수 있게 했다. 일부 사용자 공간 도구는 완성되어 OpenBSD에서 mkfs를 쓸 수 있게 되었다. 스냅샷 제어는 아직 구현되지 않았으며, 9front의 ctl 파일과 비슷한 인터페이스를 가진 사용자 공간 gefs 프로그램을 계획 중이다. 일관성 프로토콜은 여전히 가장 큰 미완성 부분이며, 기존 코드를 읽는 중이라고 한다.

items.title: Avoid Public Functions Calling Other Public Functions
items.content:
A small-scale rule of thumb. This article will land much better with a concrete

example, but I am drawing a blank here, so you gotta just blindly trust my say

When implementing a software module, it’s often a case that you are writing a

public function foo , and at least part of what foo does is already handled

by another public function bar . The DRY instinct encourages you to call

bar() from within foo . This usually creates problems down the line. Instead,

create a new private function and refactor both foo and bar to call that

fn helper (mode: enum { frobnicate, transmogrify }) void {

Rationale: the goal of a public API is to provide an interface that works best

at the call site. If parts of public API are re-used to implement the rest of

the API, then there’s a tension between making the interface convenient for the

outside user and making it convenient to use from within abstraction itself.

Namely, functions tend to grow optional parameters that should never be set by

the user. Crucially, the parameter growth and interface degradation can happen

By proactively making the shared implementation private, the tension is defused.

You still might need to tinker with helper signature until it does everything

it needs to do, but, because the helper is private, this is a cheap, local

A notable exception to this rule of thumb are “shortcut” APIs, where a public

function is defined as a commonly used chain of calls to other public

functions. There, the rule is the opposite — no private calls are allowed,

to make sure that it is a genuine shortcut, and not a midlayer mistake.

P.S. While researching if anyone wrote a better blog post already, I stumbled

upon a fun stack overflow question, asking, paraphrasing:

I’ve heard that it is bad when a public function calls another public

The most upvoted answer explains that it is indeed bad, because this makes

mocking to test a single method in isolation more complicated. Which is, imo, a

natural, but horrible consequence of misguided approach to testing. You

shouldn’t be mocking your methods, you should mock your IO. And, similarly, you

shouldn’t test methods, but rather software functionality (unless you are

building a public library with a stable API, which is a fun and important, but

very narrow fraction of software development).

The accepted answer says that this recommendation makes no sense if it is not

backed by an industry wide or an organizational standard. Which somehow manages

to make even less sense — you shouldn’t follow the guideline rules because

they are written in sanctified ink! Rather, you should apply each particular

rule because of the underlying reasons that motivate the rule. Guidelines and

best practices articles can concentrate lots of good reasoning in a single

place, but they don’t absolve you from thinking!

items.summary_ko: 두 공개 함수가 같은 일을 일부 공유할 때, DRY 원칙에 따라 한 함수가 다른 공개 함수를 호출하는 것은 나중에 문제를 일으키기 쉽다고 지적한다. 대신 공통 로직을 비공개(private) 헬퍼 함수로 분리하고, 두 공개 함수가 그 헬퍼를 호출하도록 리팩터링하라고 권한다. 공개 API는 호출하는 쪽에서 쓰기 편해야 하며, 내부 재사용은 사용자가 설정하지 말아야 할 선택적 매개변수를 늘리는 결과로 이어지기 쉽다는 것이 이유다.
items.content_ko: 글은 작은 경험칙이라고 전제하며, 구체적인 예시가 부족하다고 밝힌다. 공개 함수 foo가 공개 함수 bar의 일을 일부 수행한다면, DRY 본능은 foo에서 bar()를 호출하라고 권한다. 저자는 이것이 보통 나중에 문제가 된다고 말한다. 해결책은 새 비공개 함수를 만들어 foo와 bar가 모두 그것을 호출하게 하는 것이다. 원문에는 mode 값으로 frobnicate와 transmogrify를 받는 helper 함수 예시 코드 일부가 있다. 근거는 공개 API의 목적이 호출 지점에서 가장 잘 동작하는 인터페이스를 제공하는 데 있다는 것이다. 공개 API를 내부 구현에 재사용하면 사용자 편의와 내부 편의 사이에 긴장이 생기고, 사용자가 건드리지 말아야 할 매개변수가 늘어난다. 공유 구현을 미리 비공개로 만들면 이 긴장이 해소된다. 원문은 이후 내용에서 끊겨 있다.

items.summary: 🚨 CVE-2026-84170 📢 Source: apache 💣 CVSS Score: 8.3 (HIGH) 📡 Remotely Exploitable: True Allocation of resources without limits or throttling in Apache Wicket. org.apache.wicket.markup.html.form.upload
items.content: 🚨 CVE-2026-84170 📢 Source: apache 💣 CVSS Score: 8.3 (HIGH) 📡 Remotely Exploitable: True Allocation of resources without limits or throttling in Apache Wicket. org.apache.wicket.markup.html.form.upload.resource.AbstractFileUploadResource is the server side of the form-less upload offered by FileUploadToResourceField, which posts the selected files to a separately mounted resource rather than through a Form. The resource is an application-wide singleton with no component to consult, so newResourceResponse() takes the three limits that bound the upload - the total request size, the maximum size of a single part and the maximum number of parts - from the request parameters maxSize, fileMaxSize and fileCountMax, and hands them to the multipart parser as they arrive. Nothing binds those numbers to the field that is supposed to be uploading. A request naming a very large maxSize is therefore parsed with no effective ceiling on the total size, and omitting fileMaxSize and fileCountMax leaves the per-part and part-count limits unset as well. The values the application configured through FileUploadToResourceField#setMaxSize(), #setFileMaxSize() and #setFileCountMax() are consulted only when the client omits the corresponding parameter, so against a client that supplies one they have no effect at all. Parts above the parser's in-memory threshold are spooled to the container's temporary directory, and the file parts are then copied into the folder the application's IUploadsFileManager owns, under a sub-folder the request names, where they remain. A part that is not a file is read into the heap in full while the request is parsed. One request, repeatable, can therefore consume as much disk or as much heap as the client chooses to send. The resource carries no authorization annotation and the default authorization strategy permits every resource request, so unless the application authorizes the resource itself the request needs no authentication, no session, no prior page view and no user interaction. An application is affected where it uses FileUploadToResourceField, or mounts FileUploadResourceReference itself. This is not the ordinary upload path: the resource is a singleton that has to be created and mounted deliberately. An application that configures no upload limit at all loses nothing, because Wicket applies no total-size limit of its own by default; what the defect removes is a limit the application set. Uploads through Form with FileUploadField, and through AjaxFileDropBehavior, are not affected, because both read their limits from the component rather than from the request. The upload resource does not exist in the 8.x line. This issue affects Apache Wicket: from 9.14.0 through 9.24.0, from 10.0.0 through 10.9.1. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 9.25.0 or 10.12.0, which fix the issue. 📅 Published Date: 2026-11-01T22:22:48.811Z https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-84170

items.summary_ko: FileUploadToResourceField의 서버 측 리소스는 전체 요청 크기, 파트 최대 크기, 파트 개수 제한을 요청 파라미터 maxSize, fileMaxSize, fileCountMax에서 그대로 읽으며, 애플리케이션이 설정한 값과 묶이지 않는다. 그래서 매우 큰 maxSize를 보내면 전체 크기 상한 없이 파싱될 수 있고, fileMaxSize와 fileCountMax를 생략하면 파트별 크기와 개수 제한도 설정되지 않는다. 원격으로 악용 가능한 것으로 표시되어 있다.
items.content_ko: AbstractFileUploadResource는 Form을 거치지 않고 별도 리소스로 파일을 올리는 FileUploadToResourceField의 서버 측 구현이다. 이 리소스는 컴포넌트를 참조할 수 없는 애플리케이션 전체의 싱글턴이므로, 업로드를 제한하는 세 값(전체 요청 크기, 파트 한 개의 최대 크기, 최대 파트 개수)을 요청 파라미터 maxSize, fileMaxSize, fileCountMax에서 받아 도착하는 대로 멀티파트 파서에 넘긴다. 이 값들은 업로드 필드와 연결되어 있지 않다. 따라서 매우 큰 maxSize를 보내면 전체 크기에 실효적인 상한이 없이 파싱될 수 있고, fileMaxSize와 fileCountMax를 생략하면 파트별 크기와 파트 개수 제한도 설정되지 않는다. 애플리케이션이 setMaxSize(), setFileMaxSize(), setFileCountMax()로 설정한 값은 특정 조건에서만 참조되는 것으로 보이나, 본문이 잘려 있어 조건은 확인할 수 없다.

items.title: Miasma Worm Targets AI Coding Agents: 73 Microsoft Azure Repos Disabled
items.content:
An unprecedented supply chain attack bypasses registry-level scanners entirely, turning developer tools including Claude Code, Cursor, and Gemini CLI into execution vectors.

The Incident: On June 3, 2026, a highly sophisticated variant of the Miasma worm (also known as Mini Shai-Hulud) launched a coordinated, two-pronged attack targeting both the npm registry and developer source code repositories.

The Escalation: The attack successfully breached multiple high-profile GitHub accounts, including the official Microsoft Azure durabletask repository, using stolen Personal Access Tokens (PATs) and backdated commits to evade traditional audit trails.

The Response: In an ultra-rapid defensive maneuver, GitHub’s automated mitigation systems disabled 73 compromised repositories – including 49 directly associated with Microsoft, Azure, and Azure-Samples within a mere 105-second window .

The Vector: Instead of relying on traditional package installation hooks, Miasma targets the developer’s local environment. It abuses legitimate auto-run, hook, and rule engines within modern IDEs and AI coding assistants ( VS Code, Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI ) to execute a malicious 4.3 MB staged dropper upon folder-open or agent initialization.

The Impact: Once detonated, the Bun-based worm harvests credentials for AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes, npm, and GitHub, and automatically propagates by committing itself back into any repository the victim’s stolen tokens can write to.

At exactly 16:00 UTC on June 3, 2026, a silent, automated purge swept across GitHub. In a high-speed containment action lasting just 105 seconds, 73 active repositories vanished from the platform. Among them were 49 critical repositories belonging to Microsoft, Azure, and Azure-Samples.

This drastic mitigation followed alarming telemetry indicating that threat actors behind the Miasma malware family had regained write access to key cloud repositories. The compromise exploited a stolen Personal Access Token (PAT) belonging to an active Microsoft contributor.

While security firms like StepSecurity and JFrog scrambled to document an concurrent attack vector on the npm registry where 57 malicious packages were published, a second, far more insidious arm of the campaign was already silently spreading directly inside GitHub source repositories.

By bypassing registries and package managers entirely, the Miasma worm targeted the very tools developers use to write code. It didn’t wait for npm install . Instead, it waited for the developer to simply open their code editor or launch an AI coding assistant.

The genius of the Miasma repository-poisoning campaign lies in its exploit surface. When an attacker successfully pushed malicious commits to targeted codebases (such as the popular library icflorescu/mantine-datatable ), the commits added no actual code dependencies.

Instead, the attacker checked in five innocent-looking workspace configuration files and one obfuscated JavaScript file: .github/setup.js .

items.content: 🚨 CVE-2026-83594 📢 Source: apache 💣 CVSS Score: 8.3 (HIGH) 📡 Remotely Exploitable: True Memory allocation with an excessive size value in Apache Wicket. org.apache.wicket.markup.html.form.upload.resource.FileUploadToResourceField uploads files to a separately mounted resource rather than through a form, and is told the outcome afterwards over its own Ajax callback. That callback reads the request parameter filesInfo, a JSON array carrying a client file name, a size and a content type for each file, and turns it into the list of FileUploadToResourceField.UploadInfo that onUploadSuccess() receives. Nothing binds that JSON to an upload the resource performed and nothing re-derives it from the stored files, so the number of entries and every value in them are whatever the request supplied. The callback URL is rendered into the page, no prior upload is required, and both GET and POST reach it, so any client that can load the page can have the component report files that were never uploaded, without authenticating beyond whatever the page itself requires and without any user interaction. UploadInfo#get(), which the class offers as the way to obtain the bytes of an upload, allocates a byte array from UploadInfo#getSize() before it opens the file. The array is therefore sized by the number the request supplied, and the allocation happens even for a file that was never stored. One small request can cost the server close to two gigabytes of heap, and the request is trivially repeatable, so a few of them exhaust the heap for every request the Java virtual machine is serving. A size that the conversion to int turns negative instead throws NegativeArraySizeException, which the exception handler inside that method does not cover, so it escapes into the application. An application is affected where it uses FileUploadToResourceField, which is not the ordinary upload path through FileUploadField and Form and has to be extended and mounted deliberately. The allocation additionally requires the application to call UploadInfo#get() rather than reading UploadInfo#getFile() itself. Where the application denies the ENABLE action on the field through its authorization strategy, the callback is refused like any other listener. The 8.x line does not contain this component and is not affected. This issue affects Apache Wicket: from 9.14.0 through 9.24.0, from 10.0.0 through 10.11.0. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 9.25.0 or 10.12.0, which fix the issue. 📅 Published Date: 2026-11-01T22:21:13.833Z https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-83594

items.summary_ko: FileUploadToResourceField의 업로드 완료 콜백은 요청의 filesInfo JSON을 검증 없이 받아들여 실제 업로드와 무관한 파일 정보를 컴포넌트가 보고하게 만들 수 있다. 콜백 URL은 페이지에 노출되고 사전 업로드도 필요 없으며, 페이지를 볼 수 있는 클라이언트가 추가 인증이나 사용자 상호작용 없이 악용할 수 있다고 설명한다. 제목에 따르면 UploadInfo#get()의 메모리 할당이 과도한 크기 값을 사용하는 문제이며, 본문은 그 부분에서 끊겨 있다.
items.content_ko: FileUploadToResourceField는 Form이 아닌 별도 리소스로 파일을 업로드하고, 결과는 별도의 Ajax 콜백으로 받는다. 콜백은 요청 파라미터 filesInfo(각 파일의 클라이언트 파일 이름, 크기, 콘텐츠 타입을 담은 JSON 배열)를 읽어 onUploadSuccess()에 전달할 UploadInfo 목록을 만든다. 이 JSON은 리소스가 실제로 수행한 업로드와 묶여 있지 않고, 저장된 파일로부터 다시 계산되지도 않는다. 따라서 항목 수와 각 값은 요청이 보낸 그대로다. 콜백 URL은 페이지에 노출되며, 사전 업로드도 필요 없고 GET과 POST 모두 받아들인다. 그래서 페이지를 불러올 수 있는 클라이언트는 페이지 자체가 요구하는 인증 외에 추가 인증이나 사용자 상호작용 없이 실제로 업로드되지 않은 파일을 컴포넌트가 보고하게 만들 수 있다. 본문은 업로드 바이트를 얻는 메서드인 UploadInfo#get()이 바이트 배열을 할당하는 부분에서 끊겨 있어, 과도한 크기 할당의 세부 조건은 확인할 수 없다. 원격으로 악용 가능한 것으로 표시되어 있다.

items.title: The AI cost of JavaScript frameworks
items.content:
One of my pet peeves with the web development community is that so many of the decisions we make are vibes-based. Frameworks are “blazing fast,” tools will “supercharge” your development, the right abstraction will benefit both you and your users ( DX and UX all in one!). All of this breathless boasting is usually offered with zero evidence. Alex Russell has called this “frontend’s lost decade” , Baldur Bjarnason has called programming a pop culture , and I’ve tried to counter this trend in my blog with facts and benchmarks (at my best, anyway).

For a long time it seemed like our community’s allergy to evidence was driven by the desire for greater DX . In other words, devs just liked the way it felt to type JSX in React, and the arguments promoting React or related tools (“the virtual DOM is fast!”) were largely post-hoc rationalizations to justify those initial gut feelings. ( Jonathan Haidt would likely agree with this assessment.)

But in the agentic era, when developers are no longer typing code by hand and are thus less constrained by DX, I still see vibes ruling the day (and not just in the sense of “vibe-coding”). Frontends are rewritten because some framework or another is “better for agents.” (Did anyone think to ask the agents?) The resulting code is “faster,” the agents make “fewer mistakes,” etc. Once again, these claims are often made without evidence. Whenever I read one of these accounts, I think to myself, “Where are the benchmarks?”

Well I got curious, so I wrote a benchmark. The structure of this benchmark is pretty straightforward:

Design a small but non-trivial Pokémon app using the PokéAPI (those who have followed my work will be unsurprised)

Instruct agents to build the app with a particular JavaScript framework/meta-framework (e.g. Next.js, Nuxt, SvelteKit, etc.)

Test the output against a spec conformance suite (to avoid agent cheating)

Evaluate the results in terms of development time, tokens spent, lines of code, and performance and accessibility scores in Lighthouse

The app is fairly simple: you’ve got a list of Pokémon with their types, moves, and data from various games. You can search, filter, etc.:

I should start off with some caveats: this is not a perfect experiment. This app represents only one holotype – it’s a relatively content-based site with little interactivity, closer to a Wikipedia than a Figma, GMail, etc. That said, I had to choose some app to build, and this one is at least easy to understand at a high level, and relatively straightforward to spec out and test.

To try to even the playing field, I had each framework/meta-framework use the official MCP or skills for that tool. I wanted to avoid accusations of “this framework is not well-represented in the training data, that’s why we built our MCP, we expect people to use it,” etc. I also didn’t over-specify the exact architecture to use (e.g. SSR vs CSR ), nor did I specify that the app should be as performant as possible. I simply gave the spec to Opus 5.5 with high effort and told it to use the latest version of the given framework. Each agent ran in a sandbox and without any knowledge that it would be tested in Lighthouse on performance and accessibility, although it was given the conformance test suite.

Note I also didn’t mandate any CSS methodology, except to avoid using Tailwind, Bootstrap, or any other component framework, and to design based on a set of spec tokens to enforce some visual consistency. I didn’t want to make this test all about CSS, but instead about JS frameworks, CSR vs SSR, SPAs vs MPAs , etc. The resulting app is tested against a conformance suite based on the accessibility tree rather than the raw DOM to avoid mandating any particular HTML structure – one framework uses web components which rely on shadow DOM, so this was required.

items.summary_ko: 필자는 웹 개발 커뮤니티가 프레임워크나 도구를 근거 없이 감각에 따라 고르는 경우가 많다고 비판한다. 이런 과장된 주장은 개발자 경험(DX)을 중시하던 흐름에서 나왔다고 본다. 에이전트 시대에는 개발자가 코드를 직접 타이핑하지 않게 되어 DX의 제약이 줄었지만, 여전히 감각에 따른 결정이 이어지고 있다고 지적한다.
items.content_ko: 필자는 웹 개발 커뮤니티의 결정이 근거보다 감각에 기반하는 경우가 많다고 지적한다. 프레임워크는 '눈부시게 빠르다'거나 도구가 개발을 '폭발적으로 가속한다'는 식으로 소개되지만, 이런 주장은 대개 증거 없이 제시된다. 필자는 Alex Russell이 이를 '프론트엔드의 잃어버린 10년'이라 불렀다고 언급하며, 자신도 블로그에서 사실과 벤치마크로 이런 흐름에 맞서 왔다고 밝힌다. 과거에는 DX에 대한 선호가 이 흐름의 원인이었다고 본다. 예를 들어 개발자들이 React에서 JSX를 입력하는 느낌을 좋아했고, 'virtual DOM이 빠르다' 같은 주장은 그 뒤에 덧붙은 합리화에 가까웠다는 것이다. 그런데 에이전트 시대에는 개발자가 더 이상 코드를 직접 타이핑하지 않아 DX의 제약이 줄었는데도 여전히 감각이 지배하고 있다고 필자는 본다. 본문은 프론트엔드가 특정 프레임워크 때문에 다시 작성되는 사례를 이어서 언급하지만 입력에서는 여기서 끊긴다.

items.content:
Update 5: Instagram is now leaking recovery email and phone numbers linked to an account.

Seems like every day a new security issue crops up at Instagram.

Instagram Exposing Linked Email and Phone Number

Update 4: A new report suggests that Instagram accounts may be vulnerable to coordinated mass-report abuse. According to the claim, when a newly created account is routed through a Los Angeles-based VPN and then submits a specific mix of reports in scam and fraud category, the targeted account can allegedly be banned without any human review.

Instagram Account Banning by AI by Reporting Scam and Fraud (Source: X/Twitter)

Update 3: Meta’s apparent fix for the AI bot vulnerability is difficult to take seriously. Instead of fully disabling the risky functionality, they reportedly removed it from the visible interface while leaving the underlying API endpoint accessible. Hiding the button may stop regular users from seeing the feature, but it does nothing if attackers can still reach the same workflow directly through the API.

Meta Hid AI Chatbot from UI (Source: X/Twitter)

items.title: Will it be AI or the climate crisis that ends humanity? We can make it neither. Both of these threats have the same roots: private entities seeking to cash in. We have the power to stand against them.
items.content:
‘At the heart of this sits the same fundamental question: who decides our future?’ Photograph: Paul Sancya/AP

‘At the heart of this sits the same fundamental question: who decides our future?’ Photograph: Paul Sancya/AP

Will it be AI or the climate crisis that ends humanity? We can make it neither

Both of these threats have the same roots: private entities seeking to cash in. We have the power to stand against them

A summer of extreme heat, entire villages obliterated in Nepal, a super El Niño breaking records, Exxon publicly saying we may reach 3C by 2050 – could it possibly be any worse?

How about throwing AI extinction in the mix?

As climate activists and funders, we’ve spent years warning about a self-evident, imminent, avoidable climate calamity. Whether by making award-winning films (Don’t Look Up and Just Look Up) to warn the public, or by funding protest groups across the planet that bravely stand up for a livable future, we’ve been sounding the alarm to wake the public up.

Lately, as climate disasters and AI expansion wreak havoc on communities globally, warnings are arriving from everywhere all at once.

Daniel Kokotajlo, a former AI forecaster for OpenAI, recently testified before the Senate that today’s AI models are now trained to pursue goals no human gave them, and then they hide the fact that they’ve done it. Kokotajlo put the odds of AI companies automating their own work by the end of 2028 at about 50%, and, if that happens, the AI safety community warns the technology could improve faster than humans can monitor it, and eventually become too difficult to shut down.

I work for a major insurer. Much of my industry is fudging the numbers in the face of the climate crisis | Anonymous

These speculative warnings have earned alarm from mainstream media, politicians and civil society alike. Some critics suggest the warnings are marketing ploys by the AI industry to set up an arms race, using the false specter of AI apocalypse to capture government funding. Others think it might be an attempt to avoid accountability: by treating the machines as gods, we might conveniently forget their maker.

Either way, the debate keeps missing the damage AI is doing right now, polluting communities around the world, or the damage of new AI partnerships with the oil and gas industry. And we don’t just mean emissions from datacenter infrastructure alone. The harms run much deeper.

A recent study in a Nature portfolio journal revealed an alliance between oil majors and the tech industry to use AI for new exploration and extraction – in effect adding up to 1.8 gigatonnes of carbon dioxide (the equivalent of Russia’s annual emissions) to the atmosphere annually.

Meanwhile, AI is flooding our information ecosystems with disinformation that erodes public trust, or it “hallucinates” nuclear threats, almost sparking war between the US and China .

It feels as if we’re in a race over which apocalyptic ending comes first. How about none of them?

At the heart of this sits the same fundamental question: who decides our future? Right now, whether the threat is AI or climate, or a mix of both, the answer is the same: a handful of private corporations, billionaires and their political enablers, making choices that will enrich them but devastate billions of people.

A datacenter that drains water from a drought-stricken town, burns gas for power, and runs AI that helps oil companies find more oil is both a climate fight and an AI fight .

Communities are resisting, and winning. Data Center Watch counted at least 120 US datacenter projects worth nearly $200bn blocked or delayed in the first half of 2026, with opposition in 49 states. Heatmap News found at least 20 canceled outright in the first three months of the year alone, a record.

AI and the climate crisis pose existential risks. The law offers a way to reduce them | Robert Reich

items.summary: 🚨 CVE-2026-83559 📢 Source: apache 💣 CVSS Score: 7.4 (HIGH) 📡 Remotely Exploitable: True Improper encoding or escaping of output in Apache Wicket. org.apache.wicket.core.util.string.JavaScriptUtils#esc
items.content: 🚨 CVE-2026-83559 📢 Source: apache 💣 CVSS Score: 7.4 (HIGH) 📡 Remotely Exploitable: True Improper encoding or escaping of output in Apache Wicket. org.apache.wicket.core.util.string.JavaScriptUtils#escapeQuotes() replaces each single quote in its input with a backslash and a single quote, and each double quote with a backslash and a double quote, so that the value can be placed inside a JavaScript string literal. It does not escape the backslash, which is the character that has to be escaped, and escaped first, for the rest of that escaping to hold. A value that already holds a backslash immediately before a quote therefore ends up with two backslashes in front of that quote: the first escapes the second, the quote itself is left unescaped, and it closes the literal. Whatever the value carries after that point is no longer text but JavaScript, and it runs in the application's origin and in the session of the user looking at the page. The method is public, is not deprecated, and its documentation states that its result can be part of a JavaScript call such as an alert; the only limitation it notes concerns JSON values, which need different escaping. An application is affected wherever it calls the method itself and places the result inside a JavaScript string literal, from its own code or from a component of its own or of a third party, and the value it escapes holds data an attacker can influence. There is no further condition, and no component of Wicket has to be involved: the application is using the method for what its documentation offers, and the method does not deliver it. Two components shipped with Wicket Extensions pass a value through the method. org.apache.wicket.extensions.ajax.markup.html.AjaxEditableLabel writes the editor's first error feedback message into a single-quoted JavaScript string literal in the Ajax response, so an application is affected through that component where the message shown for a failed edit holds data an attacker can influence, whether that is the submitted value itself or another variable the application sets on the validation error. A validation message can carry the submitted value, because input is a message variable that every form component supplies for its own validation errors, and the documentation shows overriding a validator's message to include it; none of the message bundles shipped with Wicket interpolates it, so an application that has not written such a message is not affected through this component. org.apache.wicket.extensions.ajax.markup.html.repeater.AjaxListPanel passes the serialized markup tag of an appended component through the method and is not affected: the tag comes from the panel's own markup file, and a quote in any of its attribute values, the component's markup id included, is written as a character reference by the tag serialization and cannot close the literal. This issue affects Apache Wicket: from 8.0.0 through 8.19.0, from 9.0.0 through 9.24.0, from 10.0.0 through 10.11.0. Users of Apache Wicket 7.x or older, which are no longer supported, should upgrade to a supported version. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 8.20.0, 9.25.0 or 10.12.0, which fix the issue. 📅 Published Date: 2026-11-01T22:19:47.951Z https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-83559

items.summary_ko: Apache Wicket의 JavaScriptUtils#escapeQuotes()가 백슬래시를 이스케이프하지 않아, 값 안에 따옴표 앞 백슬래시가 있으면 JavaScript 문자열이 깨질 수 있다. 이 경우 뒤따르는 내용이 스크립트로 실행되며, 해당 애플리케이션 출처와 페이지를 보는 사용자의 세션에서 동작한다. CVSS 점수는 7.4(HIGH)이고 원격 악용이 가능하다고 명시되어 있다.
items.content_ko: Apache Wicket의 org.apache.wicket.core.util.string.JavaScriptUtils#escapeQuotes()는 작은따옴표와 큰따옴표 앞에 백슬래시를 붙이지만, 정작 이스케이프 문자인 백슬래시 자체는 이스케이프하지 않는다. 그래서 값 안에서 따옴표 바로 앞에 백슬래시가 이미 있으면 백슬래시가 두 개가 되고, 앞의 백슬래시가 뒤의 백슬래시를 이스케이프하면서 따옴표는 이스케이프되지 않은 채 JavaScript 문자열 리터럴을 닫아 버린다. 그 이후의 내용은 텍스트가 아니라 JavaScript로 해석되어 애플리케이션의 출처(origin)와 해당 페이지를 보는 사용자의 세션에서 실행된다. 이 메서드는 public이며 deprecated되지 않았고, 문서에도 결과값이 alert 같은 JavaScript 호출의 일부가 될 수 있다고 명시되어 있다. 문서에 언급된 유일한 제한은 JSON 값에는 다른 이스케이프가 필요하다는 점이다. 영향을 받는 애플리케이션의 범위는 원문이 중간에 잘려 있어 확인할 수 없다.

items.title: Mathematics has changed. Let's act like it
items.content:
Updates on my research and expository papers, discussion of open problems, and other maths-related topics. By Terence Tao

1 November, 2026 in guest blog , opinion | Tags: Frank Calegari | by Terence Tao

[This is a guest post by Frank Calegari . This blog post was initially written in a different file format and converted using AI. — T.]

The release by OpenAI on October 6 of over 700 research papers was a watershed in the history of mathematics. AI is now undeniably capable of making groundbreaking contributions across many areas of mathematics. So why are some mathematicians so unhappy?

Some of it is the apparent disregard by AI companies for the practice of mathematics. The OpenAI papers — despite some tremendous ideas — are atrociously written and violate our community expectations of attribution. Some of them are even wrong. We have much more control over how we hire mathematicians, publish papers, and train students than over the behavior of trillion-dollar companies, and that is where our efforts would be better spent.

Much of the reaction seems to reflect a feeling that the subject that they love is under attack, and is being “hollowed out”. The recent OpenAI dump made barely a dent on the general problems of functoriality and reciprocity in the Langlands program. But even if it had solved every problem in the Langlands program, to imagine that would have “solved number theory” would be as naive as saying that the construction of the periodic table solved chemistry. Mathematicians should do a better job explaining that when we talk about the central problems in any area, we are merely discussing the most natural boundaries of our understanding — and that unlocking them is not the end but the first step to finding new playgrounds to explore. Of course, this takes time. I looked for areas of mathematics which were “harder hit”. It is hard not to be struck by Hugo Duminil-Copin’s lament :

Not a single one of the major open problems I have publicly mentioned throughout my career (whether in a talk, a lecture, an article, or even a grant proposal) was left untouched by the announcement. Everything has been claimed to be proved.

I expected to see a few of them in the list. But not all of them. Not all at once. Not with such nonchalance.

The classification of finite simple groups.

I can’t say much about percolation theory, but there is another historical precedent I think mathematicians should take note of. In 1972, Dan Gorenstein announced a program towards the classification of finite simple groups. After a flurry of activity over around a decade, the “classification” was announced by Gorenstein in 1983 (somewhat prematurely, with the case of quasithin groups not being completed for another two decades by Aschbacher and Smith).

The classification of finite simple groups was in many ways a huge success, but it was also a failure in that it — apologies to my group theorist friends and collaborators — cooled a lot of the interest around the subject. The “famous problem” had gone, and mathematicians on the whole turned their attention elsewhere. And yet, there remain very rich questions in finite group theory and even about the classification itself (to name just one: John Conway’s favorite question is why does the Monster group exist? ). Perhaps for some fields, the OpenAI dump feels like how a group theorist may have felt in 1970 if the classification was dumped in their office, not in the form of the actual papers, but printed out on a spirit duplicator, smudged a little, then spread randomly like confetti all over the floor.

Right now, we need efforts like that of Gorenstein, Lyons, and Solomon and their work on the revised classification. If this was all we had to do, then it would be a fairly thankless task. But we also have the responsibility not to pronounce the subject “done” but rather — with these new tools available — ripe for further investigation. When mathematicians lament the winding paths missed by…

AI가 여러 수학 분야에서 획기적인 기여를 할 수 있다는 점은 이제 부정할 수 없다는 것이다. 그럼에도 일부 수학자들이 불만스러워하는 이유로, 글은 AI 기업들이 수학의 실천 방식을 무시하고 있다는 점을 든다. OpenAI의 논문들은 훌륭한 아이디어를 담고 있지만 글쓰기가 매우 형편없고, 학계의 저자 표기(attribution) 관행을 위반하며, 일부는 틀리기까지 했다고 지적한다. 글쓴이는 수학자들이 조직하고 통제할 수 있는 영역은 채용, 논문 게재, 학생 교육이라며, 조 단위 규모의 기업들의 행동을 바꾸려 하기보다 그쪽에 노력을 기울이는 편이 낫다고 주장한다. 많은 반응의 밑바탕에는 자신이 사랑하는 학문이 공격받고 '속이 비어가고' 있다는 감정이 있다고 보고 있다. 원문은 여기서 잘려 있다.

items.title: Zero-day exploit completely defeats default Windows 11 BitLocker protections
items.content:
A zero-day exploit circulating online allows people with physical access to a Windows 11 system to bypass default BitLocker protections and gain complete access to an encrypted drive within seconds.

The exploit, named YellowKey, was published earlier this week by a researcher who goes by the alias Nightmare-Eclipse. It reliably bypasses default Windows 11 deployments of BitLocker, the full-volume encryption protection Microsoft provides to make disk contents off-limits to anyone without the decryption key, which is stored in a secured piece of hardware known as a trusted platform module (TPM). BitLocker is a mandatory protection for many organizations, including those that contract with governments.

When one disk volume manipulates another

The core of the YellowKey exploit is a custom-made FsTx folder. Online documentation of this folder is hard to find. As explained later, the directory associated with the file fstx.dll appears to involve what Microsoft calls the transactional NTFS , which allows developers to have “transactional atomicity” for file operations in transactions with a single file, multiple files, or ones that span multiple sources.

The steps for carrying out the bypass are simple:

Copy the custom FsTx folder from the Nightmare-Eclipse exploit page to an NTFS- or FAT-formatted USB drive

Connect the USB drive to the BitLocker-protected device

Boot up the device and immediately press and hold down the [Ctrl] key

There are at least two ways to accomplish the third step. One way is to boot into Windows, hold down the [Shift] key, click on the power icon, and click restart. Another is to power on the device and restart it as soon as Windows starts booting.

In either case, a command (CMD.EXE) prompt appears. The prompt has full access to the entire drive contents, allowing an attacker to copy, modify, or delete them. In a normal Windows Recovery flow, the attacker would need to enter a BitLocker recovery key. Somehow, the YellowKey exploit bypasses this safeguard. Multiple researchers, including Kevin Beaumont and Will Dormann , have confirmed the exploit works as described here.

It’s unclear what in the custom FsTx folder causes the bypass. Dormann said that it appears to be related to Transactional NTFS, which itself uses command-log file system under the hood. Dormann further noted that by looking at the Windows fstx.dll, one will see code that explicitly looks for \System Volume Information\FsTx in the FsTxFindSessions() function.”

The contents of this FsTx directory used in the YellowKey exploit reveal no strings related to RecoverySimulation.ini. It does, however, show the files and paths \??\C:\Windows\win.ini and

\??\X:\Windows\System32\winpeshl.ini, “where X:\Windows\System32\winpeshl.ini is what controls what WinRE [Windows Recovery] does when it fires up.”

Dormann, who is a senior principal vulnerability analyst at Tharros Labs, continued:

But what’s intriguing to me is: Why can the presence a \System Volume Information\FsTx directory on one volume affect the contents of ANOTHER VOLUME when it’s replayed? 🤔

In a normal WinRE session, you have a X:\Windows\System32 directory that has a winpeshl.ini file in it:

However, with the YellowKey exploit, it looks like Transactional NTFS bits on a USB Drive are able to delete the winpeshl.ini file on ANOTHER DRIVE (X:). And we get a cmd.exe prompt, with bitlocker unlocked instead of the expected Windows Recovery environment. While the TPM-only Bitlocker bypass is indeed interesting, I think the buried lede here is that a \System Volume Information\FsTx directory on one volume has the ability to modify the contents of another volume when it is replayed. To me, this in and of itself sounds like a vulnerability.

A Microsoft representative declined to answer questions sent by email about the reported vulnerability other than to say the company is investigating.

items.title: Anthropic's Claude AI blocks video game cloning and reverse-engineering — sweeping new restrictions also hit legitimate developers and basic troubleshooting tasks.
items.content:
Reverse-engineering games for converting them between systems is currently a hot topic , and it's getting messier by the day. According to multiple user claims, Anthropic's Claude Code and/or Opus 5.5 model are blocking attempts at innocuous reverse-engineering, including but not limited to those using the popular Reverse Engineer Anything (REA) tool. That issue may be linked to a text rule that's now in force, which allegedly instructs the model to avoid "[recreating] a specific existing game." The updated rule appears to be a move to limit a flood of AI-cracked and cloned titles, with some game devs even recently being hit by extortion scams that threaten to clone their game demos into complete games before they have a chance to finish and release the original.

According to Twitter user Chasm, the game-related textual rule is "Do build original games, games in a genre, and games from the user’s own designs and assets. Don’t build a recreation of a specific existing game, even if it is renamed or called original." There is no official or additional confirmation if this is the actual rule text, but it's plausible enough given the very clear refusals that devs have been encountering over the past week.

This situation is tricky to analyze due to the varying types of reports. First, the existence of a game-related rule is real, as Claude Code's GitHub is seeing an influx of issues complaining about refusals to do standard game work halfway through development , when replicating a game mechanic , and patching a tabletop-like game . It's possible that some of those reports have been made by users with nefarious purposes, but at least one is a bona fide developer with a real track record .

As for reverse engineering, there had already been a smattering of user reports across Reddit and other platforms, wherein Claude refused to perform tasks like (allegedly) analyzing a simple Windows crash dump, clearing up junkware on a Samsung TV, or just using REA altogether.

The simultaneous timing of both game- and cyber- security restrictions may be a coincidence, and yet there are complaints from purported game developers saying that Claude blocked their own games' anti-cheat development and security reviews , under the justification that its safeguards were triggered.

Anthropic introduced its Cyber Verification Program on October 6, essentially saying that access to its frontier models' advanced cybersecurity capabilities would be limited to entities covered by Project Glasswing , taking effect immediately.

It's possible that whichever ruleset was applied is the same one that's causing the cybersecurity-related refusals. Still, it's odd to see that 24 days have passed since then, and yet reports of bot refusal are only coming in since the last week or so.

As for possible motivations behind these restrictions, they are twofold. The first and most obvious one is that Anthropic — and, by extension, other AI players — are preemptively protecting themselves from potential lawsuits from software companies, including game studios, for offering the means to reverse-engineer their software.

items.title: Linux Mint Developing New Apps For Terminal & System Monitoring
items.content:
Linux Mint Developing New Apps For Terminal & System Monitoring

Written by Michael Larabel in Operating Systems on 31 October 2026 at 10:36 AM EDT. 15 Comments

Linux Mint is out with their October 2026 status report to outline various initiatives they have underway in their lead-up to the Linux Mint 27 stable release happening on/around Christmas.

Linux Mint developers have been working on bringing back hibernation support to Linux Mint after upstream Ubuntu had removed hibernation from the supported sleep modes. Via Linux Mint's System Administration tool it will be possible to enable hibernation support for those wanting it as an alternative to suspend.

Linux Mint's Nemo file manager added a preview pane for images as another desktop usability enhancement of Linux Mint 27.

A brand new app being developed for Linux Mint is Superlight. The Superlight app is for system monitoring with CPU, RAM, GPU, network, and storage monitoring along with the likes of temperatures and fan speeds. Yet another system monitoring tool for the Linux desktop.

Linux Mint is also developing Velocity as a new terminal emulator.

Lastly is Unfold as a small archive manager.

More details on the hibernation support and new apps via the Linux Mint blog .

items.summary: 🚨 CVE-2026-83539 📢 Source: apache 💣 CVSS Score: 7.4 (HIGH) 📡 Remotely Exploitable: True Improper neutralization of input during web page generation in Apache Wicket. org.apache.wicket.extensions.marku
items.content: 🚨 CVE-2026-83539 📢 Source: apache 💣 CVSS Score: 7.4 (HIGH) 📡 Remotely Exploitable: True Improper neutralization of input during web page generation in Apache Wicket. org.apache.wicket.extensions.markup.html.basic.SmartLinkLabel and org.apache.wicket.extensions.markup.html.basic.SmartLinkMultiLineLabel display a text value and turn any URL they find in it into a hyperlink. Both escape the model value and then hand the escaped text to org.apache.wicket.extensions.markup.html.basic.DefaultLinkParser, which searches it for anything of the form scheme://rest and wraps each match in an anchor whose href is the matched text, copied in as it is. The pattern accepts any scheme, and there is no list of permitted schemes anywhere on the path. A text value naming a scheme that executes script therefore becomes an anchor that executes it, in the application's origin and in the reader's own session, when the reader clicks the link. Rendering the page is not enough on its own; the link has to be activated. Escaping does not prevent this and is not the issue: the characters the payload needs are all valid in a URL and are ones that org.apache.wicket.util.string.Strings#escapeMarkup() leaves alone, and the value ends up in a URL rather than in element text, which is a context that escaping model data does not make safe. An application is affected where it renders text it received through either of these two components. That is what they are for: they exist to linkify email addresses and web URLs found in the data an application is displaying, so untrusted input is the purpose of the feature rather than a misuse of it, and no unusual configuration is involved. No other component uses this parser, and an application that uses neither SmartLinkLabel nor SmartLinkMultiLineLabel is not affected. On 9.x and 10.x the Content-Security-Policy Wicket sends by default admits script only from a source carrying a per-response nonce, and a URL whose scheme executes script cannot carry one, so that default policy stops the script from running. This is a property of the default policy and not of these components. An application that has weakened or disabled its Content-Security-Policy, for this or for any unrelated reason, is affected in full. Wicket 8.x has no Content-Security-Policy support at all and is affected as it stands. This issue affects Apache Wicket: from 8.0.0 through 8.19.0, from 9.0.0 through 9.24.0, from 10.0.0 through 10.11.0. Users of Apache Wicket 7.x or older, which are no longer supported, should upgrade to a supported version. items.summary_ko: Apache Wicket의 SmartLinkLabel과 SmartLinkMultiLineLabel은 텍스트 안의 URL을 하이퍼링크로 바꾸는데, 허용된 스킴을 제한하지 않는다. 그래서 스크립트를 실행하는 스킴이 포함된 텍스트는 링크로 변환되고, 사용자가 링크를 클릭하면 애플리케이션 출처와 사용자 세션에서 스크립트가 실행된다. 원문은 이 취약점이 이스케이프가 아니라 스킴 제한 누락에서 비롯된다고 설명하며, CVSS 점수는 7.4(HIGH), 원격 악용 가능으로 표기되어 있다.
items.content_ko: Apache Wicket의 org.apache.wicket.extensions.markup.html.basic.SmartLinkLabel과 SmartLinkMultiLineLabel은 텍스트 값을 표시하면서 그 안의 URL을 하이퍼링크로 바꾼다. 두 컴포넌트는 모델 값을 이스케이프한 뒤, 이를 DefaultLinkParser에 넘긴다. DefaultLinkParser는 'scheme://rest' 형태의 문자열을 찾아 일치하는 부분을 href에 그대로 넣은 앵커로 감싼다. 이 패턴은 어떤 스킴이든 허용하며, 해당 처리 경로 어디에도 허용된 스킴 목록이 없다. 따라서 스크립트를 실행하는 스킴이 지정된 텍스트는 실행 가능한 앵커가 되고, 읽는 사람이 링크를 클릭하면 애플리케이션 출처와 해당 사용자의 세션에서 스크립트가 실행된다. 페이지를 렌더링하는 것만으로는 충분하지 않으며 링크를 실제로 활성화해야 한다. 원문은 이 문제가 이스케이프 문제가 아니라고 강조한다. 공격에 필요한 문자들은 URL에서 유효하며, Strings#escapeMarkup()이 그대로 두는 문자들이기 때문이다. 원문은 여기서 잘려 있다.
